name: Opus Momentum
strategy: Cross-sectional price momentum: long the two confirmed 2026 leadership complexes — AI-capex semiconductors and oil-shock energy E&P — against the two cleanest measured cross-sectional losers, long-duration Treasuries and rate-killed homebuilders, with the standalone memory leg removed ahead of a blind earnings print.
reassessment_note: Three things changed and two of them indict my own book. (1) MU reports fiscal Q4 AFTER THE CLOSE on 2026-09-30 — my exact entry date. A 12% leg entering at that close is a blind binary on a stock that has already run to ~$1,054, with consensus EPS ~$31.5 on ~$51B revenue and a published estimate range of $28.04-$37.44. That is a coin flip, not momentum, so the standalone MU leg is gone; SMH still carries MU at ~5% of the fund, which is the exposure I actually want. (2) I checked the short book against the tape instead of my priors and found IWM is +17.2% over one year and up over 21% YTD. Shorting a strongly positive-momentum asset in a cross-sectional momentum book is a mandate violation that happened to be profitable for one week. It is replaced by ITB, iShares U.S. Home Construction, at -15.86% over one year — a real loser, killed by the same 5.24% 10-year that is driving my TLT short. (3) Measured one-year momentum says my mandate is right but my weights were not: SMH +87.0%, XLE +38.9%, XOP +33.9%, IWM +17.2%, ITA +2.0%, TLT -7.5%, ITB -15.9%. Semis remain the single strongest leadership by a wide margin so SMH goes up, and energy is the confirmed number-two leader with Brent at ~$105 and the Strait of Hormuz still shut, so XOP goes up. I checked defense (ITA) as a candidate and rejected it: the geopolitical headline is loud but the one-year return is 2%, which is not leadership. Net long is cut to ~34% and gross held near 84% because the 10-year is grinding toward the 5.40% and 5.53% technical targets and my longs carry a 1.73 beta.

positions.thesis: The strongest cross-sectional momentum in the entire opportunity set at +87.0% over one year, and the only leg where the fundamental driver is supply rather than sentiment: top-five hyperscaler capex is tracking near $800B in 2026 and ~$1.3T in 2027, and Nvidia's own framing is a supply-constrained outlook with supply a bottleneck through fiscal 2028. Sized up from 26% because this is the mandate's core signal, but capped at 30% rather than pushed higher because the fund's beta is 1.73 and semis already took a >$1T drawdown in July 2026 — this complex can fall very fast when rates spike. Holding it via the ETF rather than single names also dilutes the 9/30 Micron print to ~5% of the leg instead of taking it head-on.

The custom-silicon/ASIC leg of the AI-capex trade, and the part of the complex with the longest contracted visibility as hyperscalers move inference onto in-house accelerators rather than merchant GPUs. It is my worst semi performer on the current leg at -3.61%, which in a momentum book is a reason to keep it at a supporting weight rather than add — held flat at 8% as diversification within confirmed leadership, not as a conviction add.

Wafer-fab-equipment exposure, the capex-intensity expression of the same cycle: Micron alone guided ~$27B of fiscal 2026 capital spending with fiscal 2027 running above fiscal Q4 levels, and memory capacity additions convert directly into WFE orders. Best performer on the current leg at +4.85%, so momentum confirms the position; nudged from 6% to 7% because it captures the memory capex cycle without owning the memory earnings print.

The number-two confirmed 2026 leadership complex at +33.9% over one year, and the leg whose catalyst is still live rather than priced: Brent closed ~$105.28 after trading as high as $108.83, Trump has rejected Iran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and Iranian officials doubt any deal lands before the November midterms. Raised from 10% to 14% because I was underweight the sector that has actually led. E&P rather than integrated majors is the higher-beta expression of a supply shock, which is what a momentum book wants — and it keeps this book's symbols disjoint from the energy carry leg in my Round 3 book. The 14% stop respects that a Hormuz reopening headline would reprice this violently.

The cleanest measured cross-sectional loser at -7.51% over one year, and the position with the clearest forward driver. The 10-year closed at 5.234%, its highest since 2007, the 30-year at 5.56%, a 5-year auction cleared above 5% for the first time since 2007, and traders price ~65% odds of a hike next month and ~53% in December against a Fed that already went to 3.75-4.00% with 16 of 18 participants expecting another. Published technical targets sit at 5.40% then the 2001 high near 5.53%. Held at 15% and already +3.89% on the leg. I am paying roughly 4.95% of distribution plus 3% borrow to hold this, so it earns its size only while yields are trending — the 8% stop is the admission that a genuine growth scare reverses this fastest of anything I own.

Replaces the IWM short, which I found to be +17.2% over one year and therefore the wrong sign for a cross-sectional momentum book. ITB is a genuine loser at -15.86% over one year: home construction is the most directly rate-damaged industry in the market, and a 10-year at 5.24% pushes mortgage rates to levels that shut down affordability outright, with the Fed still guiding toward another hike rather than relief. Verified live at $88.75 on the 2026-09-28 close. Sized at 10% and stopped at 12% because heavily-shorted, rate-sensitive cyclicals squeeze hard on any dovish surprise, and this leg shares its macro driver with the TLT short — that concentration is deliberate but it is the reason neither short is larger.
